To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

stimulation of group I mgluRs with (S)-(3,5-dhpg) (10 microM, for 2h) in organotypic rat hippocampal slice culture resulted in a significant upregulation of the gene expression of the small gtpase rab5b associated with endocvtosis, and a significant downregulation of the expression of genes associated with cell adhesion, synaptic excitation, cell death, inflammation and transcription.

stimulation of group I metabotrophic glutamate receptors protects hippocampal cells from NMDA receptor mediated excitotoxicity and that this neuroprotection is associated with changes in gene expression.
stimulation of group I mGLURs protects hippocampal neurons against excitotoxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neuroprotective effect of the group I metabotropic receptor agonist (S)-3.5-dihydroxphenylglycinc (DHPG).
the molecular mechanisms underlying neuroprotection by mGluRs, and we are particularly interested in the role of the small GTPase Rab5B in this process.
the neuroprotective effects of group I metabotroic glutamate receptors ( mGluR s).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
activation of group I receptors leads to a decrease of gene expression.
the DHPG-induced neuroprotection is mediated via a multitude of genes and that the neuroprotective effect of DHPG is not restricted to one specific gene or protein.
the activation of group I-mGluRs leads to an up-regulation of RAB5B and a down-regulation of a number of genes involved in cell death, synaptic transmission, and inflammation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the group I mGutR agonist DHPG induces a neuroprotective response in organotypic slice cultures that is reflected in the expression of genes involved in synaptic plasticity, cell survival and cell adhesion.
the group I mGutRs are involved in a wide variety of cellular functions and the activation of these receptors may have a wide variety of effects.
the activation of the group I mGLuR protects neurons from excitotoxic death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
activation of group I receptors is a potent neuroprotective treatment that may help to identify new targets for the treatment of neurological disorders.
activation of group I receptors is not only neuroprotective in vitro but also leads to changes in gene expression that are consistent with a neuroprotective response.

activation of mGluRs may have a broad effect on the expression of genes that are involved in the regulation of synaptic activity, cell death, cell adhesion and transcription, which may help to identify new therapeutic targets.
